A mathematical result; the physical connection is still open

Follow the little arrow around the loop. It returns to its starting place, but points in a different direction. The path has left a change that the final location alone does not describe.

Mathematicians call this kind of change after a closed journey holonomy. The next question is practical: could a measuring tool notice the change? The personal path offers a separate association with change in a life.

Choose “Go round the loop.” Watch which way the little arrow points when it comes back.

Words used here
holonomy
A change left after following a closed path. Returning to the same location does not always return everything to the same state.
Read the fuller explanation

Transport around a loop can return a state with a different orientation, even when the local comparison was preserved. The mathematical question is called holonomy.

The next question is practical: would your instrument notice?

A mathematical result; the physical connection is still open

Explains how a comparison can remain valid during a journey even when the final state changes. This does not identify the material system that nature uses.

Read the full source note

The locally invariant carrier and its mirror face

Pointwise invariance, compatible transport and trivial global return are separate claims. A loop can preserve the comparison structure and still return the transported state changed. Physical carrier identification remains open.
